beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:respectful, hushed wonder][tune:fall]All around Australia, the old stories of Aboriginal peoples say the ^same thing: the sea came ^in. [act:gentle, clear][tune:fall]Where there's ^water now, there used@to to be ^land.
[d:tension][act:open, curious][tune:level]What if they're ^right... [act:wonder, slowly][tune:rise]and ten ^thousand years old?

[d:calm][act:with care, sincere storytelling][tune:fall]Take Kangaroo Island, off the south coast. [act:with care, sincere storytelling][tune:fall]One story tells how the ancestral being ^Ngurunderi made the waters rise, and cut the island off from the ^mainland.

[d:build][act:quietly impressed][tune:fall]^Geology agrees on the ^event. [act:plain, confident][tune:fall]The strait between them was dry ground in the Ice Age, and it flooded about ten ^thousand years ago.

[d:build][act:clear, a clever idea coming][tune:fall]A geographer and a ^linguist, Patrick Nunn and Nicholas Reid, gathered ^twenty-one of these stories, from places all around the coast. [act:posing it, curious][tune:fall]For each one, they asked a simple question: how ^deep is the water today, over the land the story describes?

[d:build][go:2|0][sfx:shimmer][act:explaining the trick, bright][tune:fall]Then they read@past that depth off the sea-level ^curve: a graph of how the sea rose through time. [p:0.93][act:explaining, step by step]Find the depth, follow it across to the curve, drop down to the time scale, and you get a ^date. [act:the result, measured][tune:fall]^Seven thousand to ^thirteen thousand years ago. [gap:0.4][act:the reveal, slower, awed][tune:fall]Every ^single one inside the window when the seas ^really rose.

[d:build][act:fair-minded, raising the doubt][tune:rise]But could each story be a ^later guess, made by people who saw drowned trees or reefs under the water? [act:honest, even][tune:fallrise]^Possibly. [act:careful, a second caveat][tune:fall]And many were written down by ^colonists, in ^other languages, long after.

[d:build][act:warm, a little wry][tune:level]Three hundred generations is a long game of ^telephone, where a whisper passes from ear to ear and comes out ^changed... [act:the turn, lifting][tune:fall]unless the telling had ^rules. [act:respectful, sure][tune:fall]It ^did: kin who ^checked each telling, and put right any ^slip.

[d:reveal][act:leaning in, the evidence][tune:fall]And long memory has been tested ^elsewhere, against written records@noun. [sfx:hit][act:vivid, building][tune:fall]Stories from America's Pacific coast tell of a great ^shaking of the ground. [act:vivid, building][tune:fall]Japan's written records@noun log a tsunami, a giant wave, that came from across the ocean in January {1700|seventeen hundred}. [gap:0.4][act:quiet astonishment][tune:fall]^Same night.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it, calm authority][tune:rise]The ^oldest memories on Earth? [act:the verdict, warm][tune:fall]^*Plausible*. [act:honest, a careful caveat][tune:fall]^Hard to confirm story by ^story. [p:0.93][act:fair, explaining]But twenty-one stories, all landing in the right ^window, is a pattern worth taking ^seriously.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the last word, tender][tune:fall]Some libraries are made of ^people.
